utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Stanisic Defence would like to address the Chamber. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It's in relation again to the medical situation. I spoke to Mr. Stanisic and he -- the situation is a little more complex than perhaps I indicated yesterday, in that there's two further aspects which give us concern which we wanted to bring to Your Honours' attention. Firstly, that Dr. Falkner does not appear to have been replaced, so as far as Mr. Stanisic can see or ascertain, the UNDU doesn't have a treating doctor. Certainly, he hasn't become aware of such. And, secondly, in relation to the reporting doctor, Mr. Stanisic is concerned that the reporting doctor doesn't have the available information, hasn't familiarised himself with the available information about Mr. Stanisic's health. Obviously the two aspects which I raise are interconnected. If there is no treating doctor, then it's difficult to see where the reporting doctor is obtaining his information to be able to form the conclusions that he purports to form on a weekly basis. So there are the two principal concerns, no treating doctor it appears and a reporting doctor who, because of that and because of his newness, isn't apprised of the relevant information. So I raise that and put that on the record for Your Honours' consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jordash. I will take care that what you just said will be part of the inquiries which will be made on behalf of the Chamber which are scheduled to start already today.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, could I -- a point for clarification, if I may. Apparently there is a treating doctor but he has only just arrived in the last week or two. So the concerns remain the same, the newness of both now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Jordash. I hope that we'll be able to address the matter and if not tomorrow, then since most likely we are not sitting the rest of the week, there will be ways found to communicate with the Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And whether it will be the Chamber or whether it will be those responsible for the medical care is a second matter, but the Chamber keeps a close eye on it. Then if there's nothing else to be raised, could the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Grekulovic. I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Bakrac will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everybody in the courtroom and around the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Grekulovic. I will briefly look at one part of your statement. In paragraph 23 when you spoke about Arkan, you stated that to your best recollection Arkan didn't have anything to do with the forces of the MUP of Serbia present in the Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us now look at -- or rather, you said in paragraph 12 that during your stint in the Republika Srpska, the forces under your command did not have any tasks together with the Army of Republika Srpska. You also stated that you didn't have anything to do with the Army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, with the only exception being the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The military police with regard to capturing the deserters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at a D document. D140. And then I will invite your comments, Mr. Grekulovic. D140, can it be displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The document is not long, please read it carefully. Mr. Grekulovic, this is a dispatch. It seems that it was signed by the deputy minister Tomislav Kovac on the 20th of September, 1995. At the time Tomislav Kovac was the deputy minister of what and where?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the deputy minister of the interior of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And he says here at the beginning, "Based on a decision on the RS president," was it Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who was the president of the Republika Srpska at the time?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Mr. Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is my interpretation good when I say that this dispatch demonstrates that, based on a decision of the president of the Republika Srpska, Mr. Radovan Karadzic, all armed forces in the zone of responsibility were unified, and that zone of responsibility was the zone of the 1st and the 2nd Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to the forces of the MUP of the Republika Srpska, not the forces from Serbia. There are no members of our staffs or our employees among those forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is precisely what I wanted to ask you, Mr. Grekulovic. There are two staffs here, one for Doboj and the other for Prijedor. You looked at the names, would you say that any of those names, any of those persons belong to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When we look at the staff of Prijedor, we see the name of Zeljko Raznjatovic. Is this Arkan?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And above that we can see the name of Ljubisa Borovcanin, do you know what his position was at the time?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was the commander of their Special Brigade, the Special Brigade of the MUP of the Republika Srpska. I believe that that was his position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what about Simo Drljaca? Who was he?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief of the security centre in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, thank you very much for your questions [as interpreted]. Your Honours, this is all I had to ask this witness and I thank you for the time you gave me to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Could I seek clarification on one issue. You refer to the staffs. If I read this document, then as far as the names are concerned are these the names that are designated to those staffs on behalf of the Ministry of the Interior and apparently the Ministry of the Interior of the MUP of Republika Srpska? It doesn't give the full composition of these joint staffs or is my understanding of the document wrong? Perhaps I should ask the witness that this is just who? Which persons on behalf of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska will participate in such a joint staff, not the full composition of that staff; is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I believe that these are only men from the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska who were members of the joint staffs with the army. This is the way I understand this document. These are only the names of the representatives of the staffs who joined from the MUP of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, Mr. Bakrac, I have difficulties in understanding your question at page 5, line 3 and following. You say these are two staffs, reference is certainly made to two joint staffs, and that the names there are the ones designated by the RS Republika Srpska MUP, not anything else. Is that -- so these are --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are right. However, I believe that you have just clarified everything with the witness. The witness answered your question. These are representatives of the staff that the deputy minister of the interior of the Republika Srpska appointed on behalf of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska. This document does not include the names of the representatives of the Army of the Republika Srpska who also joined those staffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And also not any other person?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I agree. However, my intention and my thesis was that the Serbian volunteers and Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, placed themselves under the command of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska and that's why they were appointed as members of the staffs, and that was the essence of my question and that was the essence of the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. That has been clarified. Mr. Weber, are you ready to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Grekulovic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. You may begin, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Grekulovic. Before we begin today I just want to inform you that the Prosecution in this case does not contest that forces of the Serbian MUP were present in Bosnia-Herzegovina in September and October 1995, and that these forces included PJP units from the MUP of Serbia. With that being said, I do have a number of items I'd like to discuss with you. I have prepared specific questions, most of which can be answered with either a yes or a no. If I would like some clarifications of names, places, dates or events, I will ask you a more broad question, and as you've seen the Chamber may do so as well. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would like to start with you today by asking some clarifying questions with respect to your statement. In paragraph 6 you discuss a meeting between yourself, Obrad Stevanovic, and Radovan Stojicic, Badza. The Defence discussed the same paragraph with you yesterday. The paragraph of your statement states: "In late August 1995, Colonel Obrad Stevanovic, at that time commander of all PJPs, and I were summoned for a meeting at Radovan Stojicic's, aka Badza." My question is where were you and Obrad Stevanovic coming from?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were at work. I was in my office and Obrad Stevanovic was invited from Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say you were at your work, where was that at that time in late August 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in Kneza Milosa street at number 103 in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Since Obrad Stevanovic was coming from Slavonia, how many days before the meeting did you learn that there would be such a meeting with Badza?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned on the day, perhaps half an hour before the meeting itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this paragraph you state that the meeting occurred at Radovan Stojicic's. What precise location are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His office, in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct then that you regularly worked in the same location as Radovan Stojicic throughout 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was anyone else present for this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two of us were invited and later on we were joined by Vlastimir Djordjevic, but as I say, he only joined us later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Djordjevic present for your conversation concerning the assignment of tasks to you and what you would be doing in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the reason that he came to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time he was the chief of the police administration. He probably joined us because we were discussing the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You describe Obrad Stevanovic as a colonel in your statement. Is it correct that military ranks were being used by the Serbian MUP in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. As a matter of fact, I'm not sure, maybe they did have their own ranks. However, I don't know whether they were called colonels or chief police inspectors, I'm not sure. Ranks were introduced at some point in time but I don't know exactly when. First they had certain designations and then that was transformed into ranks, but I don't know when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, when do you recall Obrad Stevanovic first becoming a colonel?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, I did not hear that Obrad Stevanovic was Colonel. I believe that he was the chief police inspector. That was a job title, but at the level of colonel. In the statement that was recorded like that, the first rank that Obrad Stevanovic ever received was the rank of general.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 6 of your statement you also state: "At the meeting we were informed about the task." Yesterday you also discuss this at page 68 and 69 of the temporary transcript where you indicated that Badza told you that police officers from the Special Police Units needed to extend assistance to the MUP of Republika Srpska in policing works because they had a lot of refugees and a lot of security problems. I'd like to ask you a little bit more detail about those security problems. Is it correct that Stojicic told you that Republika Srpska was facing problems and was being attacked by Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me that. He spoke about tasks that we would be carrying out and that was to extend assistance to the MUP of Republika Srpska. He spoke about those tasks chiefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, did he also inform you that there were deserters, and the VRS were deserting from the front lines?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did mention that but nothing specific was told us at that time. He only explained the situation to us and he told us that they needed help, and that it was our task to help them with providing security in terms of police tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Badza told you that the Republika Srpska MUP had insufficient forces to deal with the situation they were facing?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not say that, not in so many words. He only said that they needed assistance, that they sought assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this meeting you learned that Obrad Stevanovic would not be available because he was going back to Slavonia; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You learned at the meeting that the co-ordination of Serbian MUP forces would go through Dragan Filipovic and the Serbian DB; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that he would provide any assistance we should need in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This might be an obvious question, but that was approved with the Serbian State Security Service; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know about that level. I really don't know who approved it. I only received my tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the sending of Serbian MUP forces had been agreed upon and authorised prior to the meeting?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either, but I believe so. I don't think that anybody did it on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that this authorisation was from President Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that Badza, himself, could not undertake this action?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that he made that decision himself given the level of decision-making.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Why do you believe that the authorisation came from President Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think it came from President Milosevic, but I suppose that it came from the top ranks of government. I really never was involved in that level or rather at that level of decision-making. I only believed that the decision was made up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who was part of this top-level decision-making?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Talking about the State Security Service of the MUP, it was Radovan Stojicic, and then of course there was the minister on behalf of the ministry and the minister's name was Sokolovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The transcript reflects you just saying the State Security Service of the MUP, it was Radovan Stojicic, should that read that talking about the public security service of the MUP it was Radovan Stojicic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it should read. He was a chief of public security, not chief of state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Radovan Stojicic and Minister Sokolovic would have had to get the approval of other senior officials who were sending personnel to Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was so but I repeat, I was not present at that level so I don't know for sure, but I assume that it was because that's the way it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These higher-level meetings occurred well before the meeting that you had with Radovan Stojicic; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when the meetings were held. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Grekulovic, you are a senior MUP official. The laws didn't authorise members of the Serbian MUP to operate outside Serbia. That was a job for the federal MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, but it was possible for the federal MUP to request assistance from the MUP of the republic. I don't know, however, if they did in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to a couple of other sections of your statement. At the end of paragraph 7, you describe events that occur after the meeting with Badza in late August and state: "I too was supposed to go to Pristina, but I could not go because of other commitments." What were your other commitments at the end of August and the beginning of September 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Obrad and I were supposed to go to Pristina, but I had private commitments and in a couple of days a transfer was expected so I made a request to be spared that time due to my private commitments and Obrad to go instead of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How long were you occupied by these private commitments? I'm not asking you at this time to state what the private commitments are.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took me a day or two to take care of these private commitments and we were sent off to execute our task in two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 13 of your statement, you indicate that forces under your command were: "... were deployed in carrying out tasks in several towns in Republika Srpska." And you named the locations. These locations were Doboj, Teslic, Banja Luka, Prijedor, Sanski Most, and Mrkonjic Grad. None of these municipalities are located on the Croatian-Bosnian border. Is it correct that your PJP units were not deployed at the border because this area was not a part of your assigned tasks?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yesterday at pages 81 and 82 there was some discussion about a DB operative who was assigned with you by the name of Dujovic. On page 86 of yesterday's transcript, you stated that Dujovic was with you all of the time. Is it correct that a member of the State Security Service was assigned with you throughout your time in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was with me as a liaison officer. I stated that yesterday. He was a liaison between me and Mr. Filipovic. He was there throughout the time that I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Dujovic's first name?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know, but they called him Duja and his last name is Dujovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the entire time that you were with him did he not convey to you what his full name was?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that, but it's been 17 years. I haven't seen the man since and I really don't know all of his personal details. I don't know his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Dujovic's official position in the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did he not tell you that?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not. We never spoke about it, nor did I inquire about the positions in state security. I didn't care either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Dujovic look like in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was young, shortish, thin. His looks were decent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is there anything about him that you recall that is distinguishing? His hair colour? Anything?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His hair colour, I think he had brown hair. Actually, I don't think, I'm sure. He had a receding hairline and I don't know what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It was your understanding that he was a subordinate of Mr. Filipovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood that he was his co-worker and probably a subordinate. He was the person with whom -- through whom I liaised with Mr. Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, what did Mr. Dujovic call Mr. Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He called him Fica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 18 of your statement, you state: "Dragan Filipovic from the Republic of Serbia state security was also present in Banja Luka." And later in the paragraph you continue: "On behalf of the MUP of Serbia, his role was to co-ordinate activities of the forces of the MUP of Serbia. I did not have any particular contacts with him except when I needed some assistance or consultation regarding the use of forces under my command and the tasks that they performed." When you say Filipovic's role was to co-ordinate the activities of the forces of the MUP of Serbia, is it correct that he co-ordinated these activities with the Republika Srpska MUP?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was in permanent contact with the minister in the Republika Srpska. And talking about this co-ordination, I was told to contact him only if I needed something and possibly when I had to clarify anything that had to do with the use of our units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do I understand your evidence correctly then that Dragan Filipovic was a part of higher-level communications with the senior staff of the Republika Srpska MUP?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that aspect, but I know that he had contacts with senior officers from the MUP of Serbia and probably also with those in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's correct that he was co-ordinating these activities with Tomo Kovac and Brane Pecanac; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've also describe the PJP units being at different locations in Bosnia. Is it correct that Filipovic also co-ordinated the activities of these units at these different locations?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to the units of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia [Realtime transcript read in error "Republika Srpska"], it all went through me. Nobody issued orders to the commanders of these units. It all had to go through me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in line 13 of the current transcript page there has been a mistake. I kindly ask the witness to repeat his answer. I don't want to suggest what it should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will read to the witness what he is reported to have said and then we'll hear from him whether it's incorrect or not. Should I start at page 16, line 12, Mr. Bakrac? Would that do?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read to you, Mr. Grekulovic, how your words were translated to us. If there's anything wrong, please tell me. The question that was put to you was whether it was correct that Filipovic also co-ordinated the activities of the units referred to at these different locations. Your answer was, and please listen carefully: "If you are referring to the units of the MUP of the Republika Srpska, it all went through me. Nobody issued orders to the commanders of these units. It all had to go through me."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's been a mistake. It's the units of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, rather than of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is hereby corrected. Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 86 of yesterday's transcript, you stated that Filipovic: "Mostly made sure that the units carried out their tasks for which they were deployed in the first place. He also made sure that all the tasks were being carried out in a professional manner." Is it correct that Filipovic was aware of the tasks you received from Badza back in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably was aware but he also got that information from me but he also got it from the MUP senior officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Had you ever met or known either Dragan Filipovic or Mr. Dujovic prior to your deployment to Bosnia in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, both Dragan Filipovic and Dujovic are people I met in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P2941 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a request from Tomo Kovac dated 26 September 1995 that you comment upon in paragraph 19 of your statement. This request states: "I propose to schedule a meeting between the RS deputy minister of the interior, Tomislav Kovac, the co-ordinator of the forces of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, Dragan Filipovic, and you to resolve certain problems with regard to the commanding of troops currently under the RS MUP." Were you aware of any problems related to the commanding of troops between the Republika Srpska authorities and Dragan Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This request is sent to Ratko Mladic personally. Is it correct that the VRS was kept informed of the activities of the Republika Srpska MUP and the Serbian MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, but I believe so since I've seen this letter now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Republika Srpska MUP forces and your PJP units from Serbia both wore similar blue uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a difference in the camouflage pattern. Ours were more grey and theirs were more blue. I know that there was a slight difference between them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. With respect to the patches, they also both had the tri-colour flag on them with some also slight differences; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were differences. We had a PJP emblem with the tri-colour flag, I think, and they had also the tri-colour flag but with a cross. I don't really remember the details, but there was a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 20 of your statement you claim: "During my stay in Republika Srpska, I did not see or encounter Franko Simatovic anywhere." How did you know who Mr. Simatovic was in 1995, had you ever seen him before or had you ever heard of him prior to your deployment?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see him in the MUP in Belgrade on a couple of occasions and I knew what he looked like, didn't know the man personally. But if I had met him, I would have recognised him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Dragan Filipovic was a subordinate of Mr. Simatovic in the 2nd Administration of the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, or I wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 25 of your statement you claim: "During my stay in the territory of Republika Srpska I did not come across any members of the unit for anti-terrorist operations, JATD, or the Red Berets." How did you know he about the JATD or Red Berets in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I never met any of these units there, nor was I in contact with them but I heard that there were different special units and especially when I saw a document shown to me by the Defence, it was new to me that the unit commanded by Arkan was a special unit of the republic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the end of his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your answer. You said it was new to you that the unit commanded by Arkan, and would you then please repeat what you then said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know that it was a special unit of the MUP of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct then that before being shown documents by the Defence, that you were not aware of Arkan being a part of a special unit of the Republika Srpska MUP?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to my question about the JATD and the Red Berets. My question specifically was whether or not -- well, how you knew them in 1995, so what prior knowledge did you have before your deployment about the JATD or the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no knowledge whatsoever. I really didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that you did not see any individuals wearing red berets during your stay in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That isn't what I wanted to say. That red beret was a -- was something very popular, many units wore it, but I don't know which units were out there. I want to say that I didn't have direct contact with any such unit but I saw many people sporting red berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 594.2. This is a video still from Exhibit P281 which is a video-clip. The still is taken from the 45 second marker of the video. Is there a video still before the witness? I do not see it on my monitor. It is 65 ter 00594.2. I apologise, Your Honours, I believe that we have to release it. We will do that one second and I'll come back to it. My apologies. My apologies to Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you did not know about the JATD or the Red Berets, how do you know that you did not see them there in 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that. I said that I saw many out there sporting red berets but I don't know to which units they belonged because there were many people with red berets, so I don't know if the unit was there or wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could please try this again. Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 594.2 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the individual wearing the red beret in this video still?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This video was taken of Arkan while he was near Kljuc in Western Bosnia on the 29th of September, 1995. Is it this what you saw Arkan and his men wearing in September and October of 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they wore this type of uniforms and they also sported berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Arkan is not wearing the uniform of the Republika Srpska MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, this is a camouflage uniform. Many volunteer units that didn't belong to anybody wore such uniforms. You could purchase a uniform of this kind practically anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On how many occasions did you see Arkan between September and October 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I suppose I saw him four or five times, not more than that. I don't know exactly, but I didn't see him many times. I saw him in passing if I did. I didn't really talk to him or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did you see Arkan on these occasions?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had two or three occasions to see him at Pecanac's. I saw him once in Prijedor in the office of the chief of the centre when I toured my unit. The chief of the centre whose name was on the list, I can't remember his name, and perhaps another time in Banja Luka. In any case, we did not have any particular contact, as it were, at any of those times. I just saw him, we didn't talk. We didn't engage in any meaningful conversations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could we inquire as to the person in the background of this video still.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Grekulovic, directing your attention back to the image that's before you, there's an individual who is standing as we are facing the image to the right of Arkan; do you recognise the uniform or who this individual is in this photo?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recognise the individual and I can't say that I recognise the uniform either. The image is not that clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time would tender the video still that's before the Chamber, 65 ter 594.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections or are there?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for video still 594.2 will be P3048, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You describe that you saw Arkan on a number of occasions and that certain individuals were also present during some of these occasions, you mentioned Brane Pecanac and also the chief of the RS MUP centre that you mentioned earlier. Were any of these occasions meetings?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not attend any meetings that were also attended by Arkan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could I go back to two of the answers the witness gave. Mr. Grekulovic, you were asked about seeing people with red berets and you said when asked that you didn't see JATD or Red Berets and how you knew that you didn't see them, then you corrected the understanding of Mr. Weber and you said, no, that's not what I'm saying, I said I saw many out there sporting red berets, but I don't know to which units they belonged because there were many people with red berets, so I don't know if the unit was there or wasn't. Now, a few moments after that you were asked about Arkan and his men, what they were wearing in September and October of 1995. You said, yes, they wore these type of uniforms and they also sported red berets, which means that the full answer to the previous question was that you saw many people with red berets and that you were unable to know what units they belonged to but that you knew that Arkan and his men, that they were wearing red berets, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I saw Arkan and his men sporting red berets, but I saw other men sporting red berets as well without knowing which units they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your previous answer was not the whole truth because what you are now telling us is that you saw people with red berets and that you were often unable to know what units they belonged to but that you do know that Arkan and his men were wearing red berets. That would have been the full answer, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I invite you to give the full answers next time. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was Arkan accompanied by his men on each of the occasions that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know the names or nicknames of any of Arkan's Men who were with him?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. They were his escorts. He was also -- he was always accompanied by five or six men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a number of questions related to your opinion concerning Arkan and his relationship to the Republika Srpska MUP. In paragraph 10 of your statement you indicate that the Serbian MUP PJP units performed their tasks together with members of the Republika Srpska MUP. In paragraph 23 of your statement you state: "To the best of my knowledge Arkan had nothing to do with the forces of the MUP of Serbia present in Republika Srpska. Likewise, I know that Arkan and his forces did not carry out any tasks together or in co-operation with the MUP of Serbia." In paragraph 24 of your statement you then state: "From what I know, Arkan was a unit of the Republika Srpska MUP subordinated to the Republika Srpska MUP. It is possible that in combat operations he was subordinated to the army too but I have no actual information about it. Personally, I had no contacts with him, but I did see him a few times accompanied by men whom I think were members of his forces. I do not know where from Arkan came there to the field, nor do I know who sent them or how many of his men his unit was made." A moment ago you explained to us that the basis of your belief that Arkan was a member of the RS MUP was based on documents shown to you by the Defence. In light of your testimony and your claims that the Serbian MUP PJP units were carrying out tasks with the Republika Srpska MUP and Arkan's Men were part of the Republika Srpska MUP, is your statement that Arkan had nothing to do with the Serbian MUP forces in Bosnia incorrect?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it that way. If the document is correct and if he belonged to the MUP of Republika Srpska, I am saying that Serbian police units were engaged in policing together with the regular police officers of the Republika Srpska and not with the units that were under Arkan's command. If we are looking at things that way, I was right when I said that the MUP of Serbia had absolutely nothing to do with the unit under Arkan's command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let me know if I distill this correctly. Republika Srpska MUP units were working together with Serbian MUP units. Arkan also was working with Republika Srpska MUP units. Because both the Serbian MUP units and Arkan's units were working with the Republika Srpska MUP, isn't it correct that there was co-ordination or involvement or some relationship between your forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, that's -- I'm going to object. There's a rather compound question. Co-ordination, involvement, or some relationship, those three descriptions can describe quite disparate things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you willing to rephrase, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just asking what the relationship is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was whether you are willing to rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the witness doesn't understand the question, I'm happy to rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer is yes, although we do not know whether the witness understands the question or not, it was an objection by Mr. Jordash. Please rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've described that it is your belief that the Republika Srpska MUP units worked together with the Serbian MUP units and also Arkan's units worked with the Republika Srpska MUP. Is it correct that there was some relationship between all three of these units, and if so, what was it?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the relationship and co-operation between the MUP of Serbia police units and the regular police of the Republika Srpska MUP existed in performing regular policing tasks. As for Arkan's unit, it did not share any joint tasks with the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. That's why I am adamant when I say that we did not co-operate with Arkan's units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 10 of your statement, you describe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, is this a follow-up on your last question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was going to follow up later with it, but if Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I leave it to you for a later moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, Mr. Weber. Could we take a break, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Grekulovic, is it your evidence that PJP units of the Serbian MUP were not involved in combat or offensive operations during your deployment in 1995? Do I understand that is what you are claiming in court here today?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 14 of your statement you refer to a SAJ unit of about 20 to 25 men. Were the tasks of this SAJ unit the same as yours and did they sustain any casualties during their deployment to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, their task was the same, to help our units if needed and there were no casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P2948. It is a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Grekulovic, what is going to be shown to you in a second is an RS MUP, Republika Srpska MUP dispatch dated 29 September 1995. This document is not one of the dispatches that you comment upon in your statement. Could you please read this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could we first seek clarification. The Kosovo SAJ special anti-terrorist unit, was that a unit in any way related to Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. That was a unit of the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The statement is not perfectly clear on that, but thank you for clarifying. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Grekulovic, could you please read the dispatch that's before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it possible to also have the translation up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this dispatch states a number of things. Included in the dispatch are the following quotes: "Lines were consolidated and heavy losses were inflicted on the enemy." And: "We have obtained information from enemy soldiers." And: "The adjacent units to the right made an advance yesterday." This dispatch then concludes with the quotation: "The police forces comprise of the 4th and 8th SOP, four PJP companies, and a Tigrovi Battalion with their respective fire support equipment. The plan for today is to go on the offensive." Much like the other documents that you comment upon in your statement, is it correct that your understanding to your reference to the Tigrovi Battalion is a reference to Arkan's Men?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that your units were in fact involved in joint combat operations, including offensive operations with both the Republika Srpska MUP and Arkan's Tigers, now that you've been able to see this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you are referring to PJP units, they were PJP units of the MUP of Republika Srpska that participated in combat. What I'm saying is that the Republika Srpska MUP also had its own PJP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were shown a number of dispatches in -- by the Defence in your statement. These dispatches just refer to PJP units. How were you able to distinguish between what PJP units belong to the Republic of Serbia? And this is the first time we are hearing of PJP units belonging to Republika Srpska, so if you could please clarify that.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain, the Republika Srpska MUP had PJP units that it engaged in combat and on the front line, together with the Army of the Republika Srpska and the other forces of the Republika Srpska MUP. Whereas the PJP from Serbia, from the Republic of Serbia MUP exclusively performed tasks of policing in urban areas together with the regular police units. Obviously we were called in because they had engaged their units in combat. What I'm saying is that those were not our own PJP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 6319. This can be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Grekulovic, this is a situation report from the CJB Doboj dated 10 October 1995. Toward the end of this report it states: "On 10th October, 1995, around 0500 hours, a fire broke out in Petrovo on the vehicles belonging to the in members of the Special Forces of the Republic of Serbia. One member of the Special Forces of the RS died in the fire. You will be informed in the next report. Defence lines of the PJP and 5th Detachment of the SPB are stable. There were no killed or wounded members of the PJP and 5th Detachment of the SPB." Were you aware of this incident which occurred near Doboj?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of it and I claim with full responsibility that I did not have any casualties. Nobody was injured, nobody was killed, no vehicle was damaged, no single piece of equipment that the unit had brought from Serbia was damaged. I claim this with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, this situation report indicates that a vehicle from the Republic of Serbia was damaged. Is it your evidence then if you did not know of this incident that this vehicle did not belong to your forces, but could have belonged to another force of the Republic of Serbia MUP?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The vehicle did not belong to us, I'm sure of that. I really don't know whether it belonged to any other formal structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the SPB is a special battalion of the Republika Srpska MUP?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I'm really not familiar with the abbreviation, but, yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 10 of your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honours, before doing that, the Prosecution would tender this as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Madam Registrar. Before, I did not hear of any objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, I was just distracted momentarily. No objections.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6319 will become P3049, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 10 of your statement you indicate that the responsibilities of PJP units included controlling the check-points and bringing in deserters from the VRS and MUP. Is it correct that you were referring to deserters from the Republika Srpska MUP in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant all deserters from the armed forces of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For clarity, does that include the VRS and Republika Srpska MUP?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't know that anybody was brought in from the MUP of Republika Srpska, any deserters, I suppose that they dealt with that themselves. I know that we -- people who were brought in were conscripts and deserters who failed to respond to mobilisation calls with the military police and the MUP of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Arkan's Men were present at the check-points and also brought in deserters from the VRS?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. However, those were early days when we first arrived, they did that. And after that an order was issued that that task should be taken over with the regular forces of the police of the Republika Srpska, with the military police with our assistance. Arkan's Men were no longer allowed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would just like to understand the timing of that. Is it your evidence then that Arkan's Men were present at the check-points in September 1995 when you first arrived?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we first arrived they did that for a few days, a couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it your evidence then that Arkan's Men did not continue to operate the check-points into October 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information for October. I know that when they did that there were problems in the area of Prijedor and those problems involved Arkan's Men and some military units. A problem was created and after that they were no longer allowed to do that. It was us who did that so I don't have that information for the month of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek clarification there. You say they were not allowed to do it. You earlier said they were, I think they were ordered -- an order was issued that the task should be taken over with the regular forces of the police of the Republika Srpska and military police with your assistance. Now, you say I have no information about October but what you say upon our arrival they were there and then they were ordered to stop to do that. Now, did they stop doing it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They stopped working at check-points and I know that they no longer did that. I can say that things were sporadic or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the answer is a bit unclear. I asked you whether they stopped, you said they stopped working at check-points and I know that they no longer did that. So you have the information for October, they were not there anymore at the check-points. Then you continue your answer by saying, "I can say that things were sporadic or something like that," which is a rather vague expression. Do you allow for the possibility that they still, sporadic or not, have been at check-points during the month of October, or are you certain that they were not anymore at any check-point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure that they were not at our check-points. Whether they had their own check-point unbeknownst to me, it's possible, I can concede to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your previous answer they stopped working at check-points and I know that they no longer did that, you intend to say they were no longer at check-points where we were and I know that they did not perform any tasks at the check-points we were involved in; is that how I have to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber. But no, I have one further question on a matter. You were asked about bringing in deserters. If I read your statement where you describe the tasks, and I start halfway, general crime prevention, persons, vehicles, and goods check, prevention of smuggling as well as preventing regular forces, and then between brackets, Republika Srpska army and MUP from deserting, it's being -- bringing in the deserters. Now, you said I do not know exactly, we never brought in any MUP deserters, but you clearly describe the MUP as part of the regular forces and your task of preventing members of the regular forces from deserting. Now, whether you ever found one, was it your task to do so, as you describe it here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We were instructed to bring in each and every deserter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Including if they were MUP members, the MUP members being part of the regular forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, including all members who deserted from their units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Including MUP members, that was what my focus was on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 6281. This can be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Grekulovic, before you is an RS MUP, Republika Srpska MUP dispatch from Prijedor CJB in October 1995. It indicates that members of the Republika Srpska MUP brought in about 800 VRS members who had deserted from the front and the operation was carried out with Arkan's volunteer guard. Is it correct that Arkan's Men were, in fact, carrying out the tasks of bringing in deserters from the check-points into October 1995 while your units, the PJP units, were also assigned to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these are not PJP units from Serbia. This incident, as I've already told you, happened in Prijedor. Arkan's unit together with a military unit -- actually, they clashed, the two units clashed. They were brought in, their heads were shaved, and that created a problem. The document that was shown to me by the Defence which was Mr. Mladic's letter was a letter of complaint about that incident, so the incident did not happen at a check-point. What this was all about was the bringing in of an entire unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were aware of Arkan's Men doing this while you were in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that particular incident. I heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Serbian MUP PJP units never sought to arrest Arkan while they were deployed in Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not within our purview and not only that, we were not able to do that in the situation as it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 6281 as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 6281 will receive number P3050, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3050 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, since you claim, "I do not know where from Arkan came to the field," I have a number of questions to you about your knowledge of Arkan prior to your deployment in 1995. First, are you aware that Arkan had multiple convictions for crimes committed in Serbia which date back to when he was a juvenile in 1966 and continuing through 1986?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For Chamber, cross-references can be found in Exhibit P1646.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I know that. Every police officer in Serbia knows that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So is it correct that you were aware that Arkan had a long-running criminal history in the Republic of Serbia before 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, was elected as a deputy to the Serbian parliament in December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that he was elected from the 9th District in Pristina from the province of Kosevo?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly speaking, I don't know that. I know that he was elected deputy, but I don't know that it was that district.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you know that he was elected from the province of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I know that he was elected, but I don't know in which constituency.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Serbian MUP provided security to members of the Serbian parliament?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This would have included uniformed officers from public security and also plain-clothes officers from the Serbian DB; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the parliament is secured by public security, both within and on the outside. Inside parliament they are in plain clothes, whereas outside they wear uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And State Security Service also had responsibilities with respect to providing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, your first question was about members of the Serbian parliament and the answer was about the parliament. Security provided to members of parliament outside the parliamentary building. Was that provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Members of parliament don't -- are not provided security except in situations when it's estimated that their personal safety is in jeopardy. In other words, when the State Security Service makes such an assessment, then the minister decides whether protection is provided for them or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if such protection is provided, is it by uniformed or by plain-clothed officials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By plain clothes officials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. At this time I would ask Mr. Laugel to please show 65 ter 6314. This is a video excerpt from ERN V000-3213, time-code 2 hours, 2 minutes, 57 seconds to 2 hours, 4 minutes, 31 seconds. The total duration is approximately 1 minute and 34 second clip. The transcript of this video-clip has been provided to the booths as clip 1. Sir, if you could please watch this video.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "This is how Serbs salute. The Americans have their American dream, the French have theirs, the Italians theirs and we Serbs also have the right to dream. I and you too probably have my own Serbian dream about the United States of Serbia. You saw that Germany reunited, although it caused the greatest evil to the entire world, especially to us Serbs, I don't need to point that out. They reunited and nobody had anything against it. Why are they then opposing our unification into one state? Because we are one people, we celebrate the same holidays, we speak the same language, and we have the right to create the United Serbian states. The United States of Serbia."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not rising to object. I would just ask Mr. Weber to provide us with a time reference as to when this speech was made and where before he asks his following question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, if you are in a position to meet the request of Mr. Bakrac, you are invited to do so. If you would rather leave it to a later moment in time, in view of your line of questioning, you are allowed to do so as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was going to do so as part of my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you just viewed an excerpt from a speech Arkan gave on the 13th of December 1992 before the Serbian Assembly, did you recognise the logo of Radio Television Serbia from Belgrade in the upper right-hand corner of this broadcast?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the quality of the video-clip was poor and I couldn't tell whether it was the RTS Logo. If it was the RTS Logo, then it may have been broadcast on RTS but I couldn't tell by watching this video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you need to see it again? I can show it to you if you want to look at it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please just have the first couple of seconds of the video played. And sir, I'd ask Mr. Laugel to just pause it a couple of seconds into the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, Your Honours, but since Mr. Weber is asserting that this took place in the Serbian Assembly, I kindly ask the witness to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber has put something to the witness. If there's any reason to challenge that, I think we are in cross-examination at this moment, you have an opportunity to do so. Let's first follow the questions of Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber, the short clip and then to be stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. If we could please replay the initial portion of 65 ter 6314.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, we are paused at 5 and a half seconds into the video-clip. Directing your attention to the upper right-hand corner, do you recognise that as the logo of the Radio Television Serbia from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, were public speeches from Arkan before the Serbian Assembly considered extremist or viewed as a threat to the security of the republic by the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time there were several speeches of this kind so that it would more likely be considered extremist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Serbian MUP took no actions against Arkan in relation to these speeches?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders the video-clip under 65 ter 6314.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Objection. Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, objection, but I haven't heard the grounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, the objection is that this is new evidence. There's no proper basis, in our submission, for putting it to this witness other than to add to the Prosecution case. This didn't elicit any evidence which couldn't have been elicited by the asking of questions about Arkan's speeches. Secondly, it's very unclear what the probative value of this is supposed to be. Is the Prosecution saying this speech took place in front of the Serbian Assembly? That's been left somewhat vague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree that it has been put to the witness but there's no clear answer of the witness about location and time. That's for certain, and Mr. Weber has apparently refrained from asking specific questions on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But, secondly -- I am sorry, thirdly, what is it the Prosecution are suggesting was the action that the Serbian MUP should have taken? Are they suggesting that this speech breached a particular law and if so what were the Serbian MUP's powers in terms of taking action? Are we just left with what is effectively allegations which go nowhere, just allegations that Arkan is a bad man and you didn't take any action? We need more specificity in our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, could you please respond to what Mr. Jordash just raised and could you also keep in mind that the issue of the fresh evidence was dealt with very much in the context of the need to -- for the Prosecution to select witnesses and that if a witness is called by the Defence and has specific knowledge -- if there's anything to be asked from that witness on his own situation, his own documentation, et cetera, that the Chamber has allowed that, but where is the specific knowledge of this witness now called by the Defence? So could you please keep that in mind as well when answering the objections -- when responding to the objections raised by Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. First, the Defence has called a witness that claims a lack of knowledge about where Arkan came from. This brings into question what the nexus is between Zeljko Raznjatovic and the Republic of Serbia. Because he is claiming a lack of knowledge, the Prosecution of course, has multiple ways that it could attempt to confront or cross-examine the witness relating to what was known. One of the best vehicles for doing that is using what were public broadcasts and publicly known information available to the Prosecution. That is why we have selected a public broadcast on Serbian TV to confront the witness about. The witness has, second, identified that he did have personal knowledge of Arkan being a member of the Serbian parliament from December 1992 onward. So the Prosecution has established knowledge of the witness that Zeljko Raznjatovic was a member of the Serbian parliament. Based on that, I do have further questions about his relationship to the Republic of Serbia. I will eventually revisit his opinion concerning his lack of knowledge about where from Arkan came. Third, the Prosecution put to this witness very specific questions about how the speech or how speeches were viewed, whether they were extremist or not. The reason for is this triggered by the Defence case. The Defence has asserted Operation Thomson, an operation that was conducted by both the public security and State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia. This does not originate from the Prosecution's case. As part of this contest for Operation Thomson, I now have official, a rather senior official, from the public security service of the Serbian MUP. I'm putting to him questions that both relate to confronting the witness with his own personal knowledge as to where Arkan came from and, two, what the Serbian MUP did in relation to the public comments and views that were expressed by Zeljko Raznjatovic at the time, which he said is nothing which bears directly on the defence that was raised by the Stanisic Defence. Lastly, the Prosecution would note that the Simatovic Defence is going to be bringing a witness here in a few weeks that was a member of the Serbian National Assembly and also is going to be testifying in relation to these matters. This is not something that the Prosecution could have known prior to receiving the exhibit lists. So these are the reasons that such a video like this is triggered at this time. I believe the Prosecution has a good-faith basis in light of the Chamber's guidance and we ask that it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm not sure I follow much of that but what I would submit is that the witness puts forward in his statement that he did not know in the context of 1995 where from Arkan came there to the field nor did he know who sent him or how many men his unit was made. And then my learned friend puts a speech from 1992, allegedly, suggesting that in some way there's a nexus between those two things. It's not -- it's absurd in our respectful submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two lines, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a part of a series of cross-examination, I asked about the criminal history of 20 years, I asked about this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute about the criminal record? Is there any dispute about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There's no dispute about the criminal record, theres' no dispute that Arkan made inflammatory speeches and there's no dispute that he was a member of the Assembly in 1992. This is simply, in our submission, an attempt by the Prosecution to keep adding on the most spurious of bases.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to finish, I'm going to continue through to 1995 with materials and then -- then in relation to his comment that he is claiming a lack of knowledge as to where he came from, I'm going to suggest to him something quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But he is not claiming that he doesn't know who Arkan was. He is claiming he didn't know where he came from to Sanski Most and Banja Luka in 1995. He is not -- my learned friend's proposition suggests that what he is now going to do is elicit evidence of any kind he can about Arkan and his notorious activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is granted. The video will not be admitted into evidence because the matter is not in such relation with the examination-in-chief that that could be the basis for asking these specific questions, that is, a speech in 1992 in parliament - if it was in parliament, we do not know yet. And, second, to the extent it may be relevant information, it is not information which could not have elicited in the Prosecution's case and even a matter arises to what extent it has not yet been dealt with in the Prosecution's case. Thirdly, part of the questions are about matters which are not in dispute as explained by Mr. Jordash. You may proceed, not to say that you cannot further explore the knowledge of the witness where Arkan came from. I would say let's carefully listen to the questions. If you come next with a video that he attended a marriage in 1993 or that he attended a football game somewhere, then that is insufficiently related to where he came from in 1992, not knowing whether he came from the field or not. Let's try keep focused on what was the core of the examination-in-chief. You may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. If I could just please request some guidance because I'm little confused as to what their position is with this witness. Does the Defence claim that no relationship existed between Arkan and the Serbian MUP, and do they also then not -- do they not dispute that the Serbian MUP did nothing to crack down on Arkan throughout 1991 to 1995? I'm confused. If that's not being disputed by the Defence, then I can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may, this is a complicated matter. It cannot be put in simple terms. I suggest that we wait until re-examination to see whether the witness is aware of the mechanism in such cases, whether deputies of the Assembly have some privileges or not. Because we cannot accept a simple proposition such as the MUP didn't do anything because it's much more complex than that and it should be further explored with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Jordash, unless there's anything you would like to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I completely agree with that. Did the Serbian MUP have a relationship with Arkan? Yes, it did and no, it didn't. Some did, some didn't; it's a big organisation and it's a complicated case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I think, Mr. Weber, that you have to continue without the guidance you were seeking. Perhaps you sought guidance which is not so easily to be given. We'll listen carefully to every and each of your questions and we'll hear whether there are any objections and then we'll decide on these matters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Grekulovic, the video that you just watched, did you recognise that as footage from the Serbian Assembly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The video is not admitted into evidence. If you want to -- so, therefore, for anyone at a later stage it's very difficult what the witness testified to because it's not in evidence. Is there any dispute about whether this was a speech delivered in parliament, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
